title: Simplify button loading transitions and normalize icon scaling across themes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple regressions and inconsistencies have surfaced after the recent token migration: icon-only buttons visually shift during loading, dark-theme outlines bleed on focus, and the loading spinner timing conflicts with small button press feedback. This ticket scopes a focused design cleanup: simplify loading transitions, define a consistent icon scaling strategy so icons don't reflow when a spinner appears, ensure motion respects prefers-reduced-motion, and produce updated specs for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) When a button enters a loading state the overall component width must remain stable (no layout shift) across size variants (compact/regular/large). 2) Icon buttons should swap the icon for a spinner using absolute positioning / overlay rather than replacing DOM size to avoid reflow. 3) Loading animation timing harmonized: spinner fade-in at 80ms, full rotation begin at 220ms; immediate feedback on press remains. 4) All motion disabled when prefers-reduced-motion is set. 5) Dark and high-contrast themes must preserve focus outline without bleed into spinner. 6) Updated CSS tokens and migration notes provided for frontend owners. 7) QA checklist produced with automated visual regression snapshots and a small Playwright test matrix.
design_notes: - Use overlay technique: keep icon in flow with visibility:hidden when spinner active; spinner is absolutely positioned centered. This keeps button width constant. - Introduce a new semantic token: button.loading-opacity (default 0.0 -> 0.0 to avoid double layering). - Define scale-preserve rule for icon assets: SVGs must have viewBox-preserve and use vector-fit:contain fallback. - Create two spinner silhouettes: spinner-compact (12px) and spinner-regular (16px) with same center anchor. - Motion timings chosen to reduce perceived input latency while avoiding jank. - Edge case: when label truncation occurs (ellipsis) ensure spinner overlays the right edge, not the label, to avoid content shift.
